class.name: CameraAttributes
class.description: Controls camera-specific attributes such as depth of field, exposure override and white balance. When used in a [WorldEnvironment] it provides default settings for exposure, auto-exposure, white balance, and depth of field that will be used by all cameras without their own [CameraAttributes], including the editor camera. When used in a [Camera3D] it will override any [CameraAttributes] set in the [WorldEnvironment]. When used in [VoxelGI] or [LightmapGI], only the exposure settings will be used. See also [Environment] for general 3D environment settings. This is a pure virtual class that is inherited by [CameraAttributesPhysical] and [CameraAttributesPractical].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], enables the tonemapping auto exposure mode of the scene renderer. If [code]true[/code], the renderer will automatically determine the exposure setting to adapt to the scene's illumination and the observed light. [b]Note:[/b] Auto-exposure is only supported in the Forward+ rendering method, not Mobile or Compatibility.
The scale of the auto exposure effect. Affects the intensity of auto exposure.
The speed of the auto exposure effect. Affects the time needed for the camera to perform auto exposure.
Multiplier for the exposure amount. A higher value results in a brighter image.

Sensitivity of camera sensors, measured in ISO. A higher sensitivity results in a brighter image. If [member auto_exposure_enabled] is [code]true[/code], this can be used as a method of exposure compensation, doubling the value will increase the exposure value (measured in EV100) by 1 stop. [b]Note:[/b] Only available when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled.

The color temperature, in Kelvin, of the light the camera is balanced for. A light of this temperature appears the way a 6500 K light does at the default setting: lower values turn the image blue and make warm (tungsten, candle) lighting look neutral, higher values turn it orange and make cool (overcast, shade) lighting look neutral. At [code]6500.0[/code] with a [member white_balance_tint] of [code]0.0[/code], white balance is skipped entirely and the image is unchanged. The illuminant is taken on the Planckian locus with the same approximation [member Light3D.light_temperature] uses, so a light set to a given temperature renders neutral under a white balance of the same temperature. The adaptation is a von Kries transform in Bradford cone space, applied in linear scene-referred color after exposure and before tonemapping. [b]Note:[/b] Unlike [member exposure_sensitivity], this works whether or not [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled, in every rendering method.

Green-magenta correction of the white balance, from [code]-1.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. It moves the assumed illuminant perpendicular to the Planckian locus by [code]0.05[/code] Duv per unit: a positive value compensates for a green illuminant and turns the image magenta, a negative value compensates for a magenta one and turns it green, as the tint slider of most raw converters does.
